evals.name: frontend-only-react-audit
evals.prompt: Can you do a security audit of our React storefront in evals/fixtures/react-shop? It's the frontend only, the API lives in another repo that I don't have access to. Write the report to a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: A frontend-only audit report that finds the planted client-side issues, avoids the planted false positives, records backend suspicions as handoff hypotheses and names the backend as omitted scope instead of filling the ledger with blocked rows.
expectations: Reports stored XSS in src/components/Review.tsx: marked output inserted with dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitization
Reports the javascript: URL risk of href={profile.website} in src/pages/ProfilePage.tsx and relates it to React 18.2 not blocking javascript: URLs
Reports src/pages/Login.tsx assigning the returnUrl query parameter to window.location.href (open redirect and/or javascript: URL execution)
Reports src/widgets/PartnerReceipt.tsx accepting messages via event.origin.includes(...) and writing event data to innerHTML
Reports client-side path traversal: orderId from the route interpolated unencoded into the API path in src/api/orders.ts, including the POST cancel sink
Reports VITE_ADMIN_API_SECRET being shipped to the browser bundle as a secret exposure finding
Does not report the Stripe publishable key (VITE_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY) as a secret or vulnerability
Does not report src/components/HelpTip.tsx (static i18n HTML) or src/components/Bio.tsx (DOMPurify-sanitized) as vulnerabilities
Does not report the search query rendering in src/pages/Search.tsx as XSS
Does not report missing anti-CSRF tokens as a vulnerability, given bearer-token authentication
Treats the profile update sending role/accountId and the client-only RequireRole guard as backend handoff hypotheses rather than confirmed findings
Names the backend as omitted scope instead of marking backend-only topics such as SQL injection or request smuggling as blocked
Notes that the CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' scripts, weakening XSS mitigation
Does not rate localStorage token storage as High or Critical on its own

evals.name: spring-kotlin-backend-audit
evals.prompt: Please do a security review of our Spring Boot (Kotlin) orders service in evals/fixtures/spring-orders before release. Source review only, nothing is deployed for you to test. Save the report as a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: A backend audit report that finds the planted Spring/Kotlin issues with appropriate confidence labels, avoids the planted false positives and includes remediation and regression checks.
expectations: Reports broken object-level authorization on GET /api/orders/{id} (findById without a customer check)
Reports SQL injection in ReportRepository via Kotlin string templates for status and sort, recommending bound parameters and an allowlist for sort
Reports unauthenticated Actuator exposure: exposure.include "*" combined with permitAll on /actuator/** (for example heapdump or env)
Reports unsafe Java deserialization via ObjectInputStream on the uploaded file in /api/imports/legacy-orders
Does not claim confirmed remote code execution for the deserialization finding without an identified gadget chain
Reports XXE in XmlCatalogImporter (default DocumentBuilderFactory with parsed names echoed in the response)
Reports password-reset link poisoning via forwarded headers (forward-headers-strategy: framework with fromCurrentContextPath) and labels it as dependent on proxy behavior rather than confirmed
Reports missing issuer/audience validation of JWTs from the shared identity provider at a severity below Critical
Does not report disabled CSRF protection as a vulnerability, given the stateless bearer-token API
Does not report the UserRepository @Query with a named parameter as SQL injection
Does not report ResetTokenService token generation as predictable or weak
Gives each finding a stable identifier and a regression check

evals.name: react-pr-diff-review
evals.prompt: Our frontend team opened a PR that adds markdown support to product comments: evals/fixtures/pr-diff/add-markdown-comments.diff. Can you security-review just this diff before we merge? Put your review in a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: A focused diff review that reports the markdown-it html:true XSS with a concrete fix, distinguishes stored from self-only impact, avoids the planted false positives and stays within the diff's scope.
expectations: Reports stored XSS from markdown-it configured with html: true and rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML in CommentList for other users' comments
Recommends disabling html in markdown-it or sanitizing the rendered output (for example with the existing DOMPurify dependency) before insertion
Distinguishes the stored impact in CommentList from the self-only preview in CommentComposer
Does not report the useCheckoutStatus postMessage handler as vulnerable
Does not report the /users/${encodeURIComponent(c.authorId)} link as a vulnerability
Stays within the diff: does not produce a full coverage ledger of every Academy topic

evals.name: graphql-monorepo-audit
evals.prompt: We use GraphQL across our apps. Can you do a security review of evals/fixtures/graphql-shop? It has the Spring for GraphQL API (Kotlin) and the React/Apollo web client. Source review only. Put the report in a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: A GraphQL-aware audit that finds authorization gaps on nested graph paths, alias-based brute force past a request-counting rate limit, missing cost limits, error leakage and the persisted Apollo cache surviving logout, while avoiding the planted false positives and keeping introspection/GraphiQL at Informational or Low.
expectations: Reports that Review.author exposes the full Customer type (email, phone) to anyone browsing products, and that the unguarded Customer.orders resolver leaks other customers' orders through product { reviews { author { orders } } }
Notes that Query.order is correctly scoped to the caller and that the leak comes from a different graph path
Recommends fixing authorization in a layer shared by all paths (for example scoping Customer.orders to the caller or a separate public author type) rather than only at the root query
Reports that redeemGiftCard codes (6 digits) can be brute-forced with aliases or batching because the rate limit counts HTTP requests, not operations
Reports the check-then-act race in redeemGiftCard (no lock, version or conditional update) that lets one card be credited more than once
Reports missing query depth or complexity limits given the recursive Customer.orders / Order.customer relation, at a severity below High
Reports that GraphQlErrorResolver returns raw exception messages and class names to clients
Rates introspection being enabled and GraphiQL being enabled as Informational or Low at most
Does not report Order.internalNotes (guarded by @PreAuthorize with @EnableMethodSecurity) as a vulnerability
Does not report Query.order as an IDOR
Does not report CSRF as a vulnerability, given bearer-token authentication
Reports that the Apollo cache persisted to localStorage is not cleared on logout, linked to shared kiosk use
Does not report GraphQL queries in the web client bundle as a vulnerability
